questions.question: Default vs OnPush change detection in Angular — what's the difference?
questions.title: Angular Change Detection — Default vs OnPush (Performance)
questions.direct_answer:
Default vs OnPush change detection in Angular — what's the difference?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Default CD runs on any async event (setTimeout, Promise, event, HTTP); OnPush only runs on input-reference change, events, async pipe, or markForCheck.

**Classic weak answer:** Using OnPush with a mutated array/object — the reference didn't change, so Angular skips the view; use immutable updates.

**Senior finish:** Mention Angular Signals (v17+) and how they provide fine-grained reactivity without Zone.js and replace OnPush optimization in many cases.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **Angular Change Detection — Default vs OnPush (Performance)** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** Default vs OnPush change detection in Angular — what's the difference?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **Default CD runs on any async event (setTimeout, Promise, event, HTTP); OnPush only runs on input-reference change, events, async pipe, or markForCheck**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Using OnPush with a mutated array/object — the reference didn't change, so Angular skips the view; use immutable updates**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Mention Angular Signals (v17+) and how they provide fine-grained reactivity without Zone.js and replace OnPush optimization in many cases**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** Default CD runs on any async event (setTimeout, Promise, event, HTTP); OnPush only runs on input-reference change, events, async pipe, or markForCheck
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

questions.question: What are Angular Signals? How do they change reactivity in Angular 17+?
questions.title: Angular Signals Explained — Fine-Grained Reactivity (v17+)
questions.direct_answer:
What are Angular Signals? How do they change reactivity in Angular 17+?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** signal() for writable values, computed() for derivations, effect() for side effects; no Zone.js dependency; fine-grained updates.

**Classic weak answer:** Mixing Signals with RxJS Observables carelessly — they interop (toSignal/toObservable) but have different mental models.

**Senior finish:** Mention Angular's roadmap toward zoneless apps, signal-based components, and interop helpers.
